text.p: Australia's beleaguered housing market has begun recovering, an industry study said on Sunday, but the upturn would be slower and steadier than previous booms.
"Overall...1996 saw a general improvement in the Australian property market," the Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA) monthly survey for December said.
"As oversupplies of housing start to be exhausted, dwelling prices have begun to rise."
The survey said house prices in Sydney, Melbourne, Hobart and Newscastle outstripped inflation in 1996.
"REIA's housing figures are an indication that the property market around Australia is beginning to improve," said deputy president John Franklyn.
"We do not expect (a) property explosion of the magnitude of the late 1980s boom," he said in a statement.
"Remaining pockets of oversupply, combined with lower levels of general consumer confidence, make it likely that this property upturn will be slower and steadier than previous booms."
Franklyn said the institute projected steady growth in most markets around the country through calendar 1997.
"Falls in interest rates during 1996 have meant that home loan affordability is currently very high around Australia," he said.
The survey found house prices during 1996 continued to fall in Canberra, Adelaide and Perth.
The survey also presented an optimistic outlook for the rental market, with rents generally outstripping inflation.
